verdict.summary: Creating your own Clio Manage app and connecting your own account is straightforward, but it needs a paid Clio account (EasyStart is excluded). Only a public App Directory listing goes through Clio's security review, demo and listing process.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for a private app with a paid Manage account; several days to weeks of active work for a public listing (depends on Clio's review and your security documents)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 minutes once a paid Clio Manage account exists (estimate, not from sources)
verdict.approval_wait: None for a private/unlisted app. Public listing: Clio's review timeline is not confirmed; a support article says it aims to review the security questionnaire within 2 business days, but that article's currency is unverified.

gates.name: Developer app in your own Clio Manage account
gates.unlocks: Create a Clio Manage OAuth app and connect your own Manage account through the authorization flow.
limits: Developer portal sign-in uses a Clio Manage account (f2).
Clio has no separate sandbox; the 7-day free trial Manage account is the test environment (f4).
Creating private app keys and secrets requires access to a paid Clio account; EasyStart does not support apps (f6, f7).
Access tokens last 30 days; refresh tokens do not expire (f16).
gates.time_to_reach: About 30-60 minutes once you can sign in to developers.clio.com with a Manage account

gates.name: Private app, not reviewed and not listed in the App Directory
gates.unlocks: A private Manage app that Clio does not review. It cannot be published in the App Directory, so it is for your own firm or accounts you control.
limits: Private apps are not reviewed by Clio and cannot be published in the App Directory (f6).
Install caps and user limits for unreviewed Manage apps were not found in Clio's docs (f36, inferred absence).
Test-user allowlists or dev-mode restrictions were not found (see open questions).
Each Clio region needs its own developer application (f10).
gates.time_to_reach: No separate step; reached when the Gate 1 app exists and is used without a listing

gates.name: Public App Directory listing
gates.unlocks: Clio customers can discover and add the app from the Clio App Directory.
limits: Listing requires a security and compliance review, a demo to Clio, and a listing form that Clio drafts (f24, f26).
The App Directory review includes a pre-recorded demonstration by Clio (f27).
You must publicly publish Terms of Service, Security Policy and Privacy Policy (f29).
Manage API rate limit is 50 requests per minute per access token during peak hours; custom increases are not supported (f33, f35).
Clio may decline a listing or block API access for red-flag practices (f29).
gates.time_to_reach: Not confirmed. Clio's stated security-review target is 2 business days (support article, currency unverified). Add time for the demo, listing form and any fixes.

steps.title: Confirm your Clio account and portal access
steps.detail: Sign in to https://developers.clio.com with a Clio Manage account. This is the Clio Manage developer portal, not the Clio Platform (Grow) portal at developers.api.clio.com. Confirm your Manage account is on a plan that supports apps; EasyStart does not.
gotchas: Platform (Grow) apps are created in a different portal and are not the same registration.
If you need a trial account, Clio does not offer a separate sandbox; the 7-day trial Manage account is the test environment.

steps.title: Get the exact Composio callback URL
steps.detail: In your Composio auth config for Clio Manage, copy the callback URL shown there. You will paste this exact value as the redirect URI in the Clio app. Composio's managed Clio app was not confirmed, so you are supplying your own client ID and secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Clio requires the redirect_uri in the authorize request to match a saved redirect URL exactly.

steps.title: Create the Manage developer application
steps.detail: Open developers.clio.com/apps/new (or Developer Apps in the portal) and create a Clio Manage application. Enter a name, website URL, the Redirect URI from the Composio callout, and any optional fields you want (description, icons, support URL, deauthorization callback). Accept the Developer Terms of Service.

values.label: Required fields
values.value: Name, Website URL, one or more Redirect URIs, Developer Terms of Service acceptance, app permissions

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Description, icons, support URL and deauthorization callback are optional.
The App ID in the app list is not the App Key (client ID); use the App Key for OAuth.

steps.title: Select the minimum access permissions
steps.detail: Choose the access permissions your integration needs, per resource, as read-only or read/write. Clio advises the smallest set that lets the app function. Permissions are fixed once a user authorizes, so decide before you test with real users.

values.label: Permissions
values.value: Per-resource read or read/write; smallest necessary set

gotchas: Changing permissions later requires users to reauthorize to receive tokens with the new scopes.
A user's Clio role can still block an action even if the scope is granted; a firm admin may need to change the role.
Calls without the needed permission return 403 Forbidden (ForbiddenError).

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into Composio
steps.detail: Open developers.clio.com, go to Developer Apps, then your app. Copy the Client id and Client secret shown there. Enter them in your Composio auth config for Clio Manage. Keep the secret out of source control and store it in environment variables.

values.label: Client ID
values.value: Shown on the app page under Developer Apps

values.label: Client secret
values.value: Shown on the app page under Developer Apps

gotchas: Composio's exact field labels for Clio were not confirmed; match them to the Composio auth config screen.

steps.title: Run a test authorization against your own account
steps.detail: With access to the app credentials, an agent can run one authorization: send the user to the authorize endpoint with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri and a state value, then exchange the code at the token endpoint. Codes expire after 10 minutes. Check that an access token is returned.

values.label: Token request
values.value: Form-encoded POST: client_id, client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri

gotchas: Use the same redirect_uri in the authorize and token requests.
Tokens from app.clio.com are not valid against EU, CA or AU endpoints.
Pasting the URL into a browser without a session triggers a Clio login page; sign in with the test account.

steps.title: Handle token lifetime and refresh
steps.detail: Build refresh with grant_type=refresh_token. Access tokens last 30 days, so expect a 401 with an expired-token error after that. Refresh tokens do not expire, so encrypt them and store them securely. Clio does not document a refresh-token rotation rule.

values.label: Refresh token
values.value: Does not expire; encrypt and store securely

gotchas: Clio's docs do not state a refresh-token rotation policy; handle a changed refresh token defensively.

steps.title: Plan one app per Clio region if needed
steps.detail: If your app will run in more than one Clio region (US, EU, CA, AU), create a Clio account and a separate Developer Application in each region. App IDs differ per region, and tokens do not cross regions. Regional authorize and token hosts are not confirmed by Clio's own pages.
steps.est_time: 30 min to decide; 15 min per extra app

steps.title: Decide whether a private app is enough (Gate 2)
steps.detail: A private app is not reviewed and cannot be listed. Confirm with Clio whether your target users can connect it and whether there are install or user caps before you rely on it. The docs do not state caps.

steps.title: Draft the public documents (Gate 3 prep)
steps.detail: An agent can draft the public Terms of Service, Security Policy, Privacy Policy, vulnerability management and patching document (with high, medium and low severity timelines), and a data-handling summary. You must review them, legally approve them and publish them at public URLs. Clio also asks for supporting certifications (for example SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS) to be documented publicly where you have them.

steps.title: Request the security questionnaire
steps.detail: Once the integration is ready, email api.partnerships@clio.com to request a security questionnaire. Clio's support article says it aims to review within 2 business days, but that figure may be out of date.

steps.title: Complete the security review and record the demo
steps.detail: Complete the security and compliance review and fix any findings. Then demo the integration to Clio. Clio runs its review through a pre-recorded demonstration of your app and integration, so prepare a clean walkthrough of the connect flow and core features.

steps.title: Complete the App Directory listing form
steps.detail: After a successful demo, Clio's API Partnerships team sends an App Directory listing form. Complete it and provide the integration-specific onboarding content. Clio makes the listing public after it reviews the form.

steps.title: Wait for Clio's review decision
steps.detail: Clio reviews the security questionnaire, the demo and the listing form, then publishes the listing. No public timeline is confirmed in the findings. Keep the app working in the meantime; Clio may block API access for red-flag practices.

requirements.item: Clio Manage account able to create apps
requirements.detail: Sign in to developers.clio.com with a Manage account. A paid account is needed for the app key and secret; EasyStart does not support apps.
The redirect_uri must match one of the saved redirect URLs. Clio's Platform docs require exact matches on protocol, domain and path; Manage does not repeat the rule, so treat it as exact.
Multi-region apps need a Developer Application in each region with its own App ID.

requirements.item: Private app is not reviewed and cannot be listed
requirements.detail: Private Manage apps are not reviewed by Clio and cannot be published in the App Directory.

requirements.item: Security and compliance review for a listing
requirements.detail: A listed app must pass Clio's security and compliance review. Request the questionnaire by email to api.partnerships@clio.com.

requirements.item: Demo to Clio and listing form
requirements.detail: Clio runs a pre-recorded demonstration review, then sends the App Directory listing form.

requirements.item: Public Terms, Security Policy and Privacy Policy
requirements.detail: Must be publicly visible. Red flags can lead to a declined listing or blocked API access.
Public document with timelines for high, medium and low severity issues.
Web apps must support the latest two versions of major browsers; desktop apps must show 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis.
Track where user data is processed and stored and meet the residency requirements of each region where the app operates.

scopes.scope: Manage access permissions (per resource, read-only or read/write)
scopes.effect: Chosen at app creation. Clio advises the smallest set. Permissions are fixed once a user authorizes; changes need reauthorization. Clio does not publish a full list or mark any as sensitive or restricted.

scopes.scope: Model scopes required for webhooks, plus a separate webhooks scope
scopes.effect: Creating or updating a webhook needs the subscribed model's scope and the webhooks scope.
Clio Payments API access requires the authenticating user to accept this scope during OAuth authorization.

scopes.scope: Multi-permission endpoints (Personal Injury; Clio Payments with Accounting)
scopes.effect: Personal Injury endpoints need the Personal Injury permission plus Matters, Documents and Contacts. Clio Payments endpoints need Clio Payments plus Accounting.
Separate product: uses account.clio.com with its own app key and secret. Not needed for Manage API access.

blockers.symptom: Cannot create the app or get a Client secret
blockers.cause: Private app keys and secrets need a paid Clio account; apps are not available on the EasyStart tier.
blockers.fix: Confirm your Clio plan supports apps and that the account can use the Manage developer portal. Contact Clio if the trial or developer account does not show app creation.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with a redirect or invalid redirect_uri error
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the authorize request does not exactly match a redirect URL saved in the Clio app.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the Clio app's redirect URLs and use the same value in the authorize and token requests.

blockers.symptom: API calls return 401 after about 30 days
blockers.fix: Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token using the stored refresh token.

blockers.cause: The app lacks the permission for that endpoint, or the user's Clio role blocks the action.
blockers.fix: Add the needed permission in the app and have users reauthorize. Ask a firm administrator to adjust the user's role if needed.

blockers.symptom: Listing review or API access is declined or blocked
blockers.cause: Missing public Terms, Security Policy or Privacy Policy, or red-flag practices in Clio's guidelines.
blockers.fix: Publish the required policies and review Clio's developer security guidelines before requesting review.

blockers.symptom: Tokens fail against an EU, CA or AU region
blockers.cause: Tokens from app.clio.com do not work on regional endpoints, and each region needs its own app.
blockers.fix: Create a Developer Application in each region and use that region's credentials and hosts.

composio.note: Composio's toolkit catalog returned no toolkit for 'clio' (lookup tried 'clio' only). No managed Clio Manage OAuth app is confirmed, so plan on your own Clio Manage developer application and supply its client ID and secret. Composio's default scopes and authorize/token URLs were not confirmed; use Clio's documented URLs (US: app.clio.com; EU, CA and AU use regional hosts) and the Clio permissions you select at app creation.

evidence.claim: Clio Manage developer portal is at developers.clio.com and is where Clio Manage OAuth applications are created; it is separate from the Clio Platform (Grow) portal.
evidence.quote: The Clio Manage developer portal is located at https://developers.clio.com and is the location for creating your Clio Manage OAuth Applications.

evidence.claim: If an app operates in multiple Clio regions, the developer needs a Clio account and a separate Developer Application in each region; App IDs differ per region.
evidence.quote: If your app operates in multiple Clio regions, you will need a Clio account and Developer Application in each region.

evidence.claim: Client ID and client secret are displayed on the app's page in the Manage developer portal once the app exists.
evidence.quote: Clio Manage: developers.clio.com → Developer Apps → Your app. Your Client id and Client secret are displayed there.

evidence.claim: The redirect_uri in the authorize request must match one of the redirect URLs saved in the app settings.
evidence.quote: The URL must match one of the redirect URLs specified in your application settings.

evidence.claim: Clio's Platform (Grow) OAuth docs state redirect URIs must be exact matches including protocol, domain and path; the Manage pages fetched do not repeat that rule, and Manage PKCE support is not documented.
evidence.quote: These must be exact matches, including protocol (http/https), domain, and path.

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint takes response_type=code, client_id, and redirect_uri (required), with state recommended; redirect_on_decline is optional and defaults to false.
evidence.quote: redirect_on_decline | When set to "true", redirects users to the provided redirect_uri when a user declines the app permissions; defaults to "false".

evidence.claim: Authorization codes are valid for 10 minutes and are exchanged at the token endpoint by a form-encoded POST carrying client_id, client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code, code, and redirect_uri.
evidence.quote: The code is valid for 10 minutes.

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 30 days (expires_in 2592000 in the sample), and refresh tokens are documented as not expiring; they are refreshed with grant_type=refresh_token.
evidence.quote: Refresh tokens do not expire; as a result, they should be encrypted and stored securely.

evidence.claim: Clio's 401 troubleshooting table lists the 30-day access token lifetime and notes that tokens from app.clio.com are not valid against EU, CA or AU endpoints.
evidence.quote: Access token has expired (tokens last 30 days)

evidence.claim: A user can revoke app access inside Clio Manage, which deauthorizes that user's tokens; the app can also call the deauthorize endpoint, and a deauthorization callback URL can be set to receive notifications.
evidence.quote: The user has revoked access to your application from within Clio Manage.

evidence.claim: The developer selects access permissions (Clio's term for OAuth scopes) per resource at app creation, choosing read-only or read/write, and Clio advises selecting the smallest set needed.
evidence.quote: You should choose the smallest set necessary for your application to function properly

evidence.claim: The Manage developer portal signs developers in with Clio Manage accounts, so a Manage account is needed to make changes to OAuth apps.
evidence.quote: The Clio Manage developer portal uses Manage accounts to sign in and make changes to your OAuth applications.

evidence.claim: Access permissions are separate from user roles: even with the right scope, a user's Clio role can block an action, and a firm administrator has to change that role.
evidence.quote: Even with the correct OAuth scope, a user can only access data their Clio role permits.

evidence.claim: Webhook subscriptions need the scope for the subscribed model plus a separate webhooks scope; the Manage API reference maps each model to a scope name.
evidence.quote: Your application needs to have the corresponding model OAuth scope when creating or updating a webhook.

evidence.claim: Clio Payments API access requires the authenticating user to accept the clio_payments scope during OAuth authorization.
evidence.quote: Access to Clio Payments API will require the authenticating user to accept the clio_payments scope

evidence.claim: Clio Identity (SSO) uses a separate authorize endpoint at account.clio.com with scope openid and its own app key and secret.
evidence.quote: scope: "openid"

evidence.claim: Clio's listing docs say a listed app must pass a security and compliance review, and that Clio aims to review the security questionnaire within 2 business days (support article; currency unverified).
evidence.quote: We aim to review within 2 business days.

evidence.claim: For a public listing, the developer emails api.partnerships@clio.com to request a security questionnaire once the integration is ready.
evidence.quote: email api.partnerships@clio.com with a request for a security questionnaire.

evidence.claim: Manage launch steps are: complete the security and compliance review, demo the integration to Clio, complete an App Directory listing form that Clio drafts for review, then Clio makes the listing public.
evidence.quote: After your successful demo, the API Partnerships team will provide you with a App Directory listing form

evidence.claim: The App Directory review includes a pre-recorded demonstration of the app and integration by Clio.
evidence.quote: Clio will conduct a review through a pre-recorded demonstration of your app and integration.

evidence.claim: Listing requirements include passing a security review and providing integration-specific onboarding content; web apps must support the latest two versions of major browsers and desktop apps must show 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis.
evidence.quote: Demonstrate at least 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis for core functionality

evidence.claim: The developer must maintain a publicly visible Terms of Service, Security Policy and Privacy Policy; Clio lists red flags that can lead it to decline a listing or block API access.
evidence.quote: Below are a few red flags that can lead Clio to decline listing an app on the Clio App Directory and/or block Clio Public API access for the App

evidence.claim: Probing developers.clio.com without a session redirects to a Clio login page on the Clio account identity service (login wall).
evidence.quote: Sign in to Clio Developer Portal US Email Next: Password

evidence.claim: Clio's security guidance expects the App Key and App Secret to be kept private and stored in environment variables rather than public repositories.
evidence.quote: Ensure the App Key and App Secret are secure and private.

evidence.claim: Clio asks developers to document any supporting certifications (for example SOC2, ISO-27001, PCI-DSS) publicly; its general requirements list certifications and a TRUSTe-style privacy certification as items that help streamline listing approval.
evidence.quote: The following items will help streamline approval for listing an app on the Clio App Directory:

evidence.claim: Clio expects a public vulnerability management and patching document with timelines for high, medium and low severity issues.
evidence.quote: Have a public document describing your vulnerability management and patching workflow

evidence.claim: Manage API rate limits are applied per access token, not per app; the default is 50 requests per minute during peak hours, with higher limits off-peak.
evidence.quote: Clio's API has a default rate limit of 50 requests per minute during peak usage hours.

evidence.claim: Peak hours for US/CA are 04:00-19:00 Pacific, Monday to Friday; responses carry X-RateLimit headers and exceeding the limit returns 429 with Retry-After.
evidence.quote: US/CA Regions: 04:00-19:00 Pacific Time, Monday-Friday

evidence.claim: Clio does not support custom rate-limit increases for applications at this time, and limits may change without notice.
evidence.quote: We do not support custom rate limit increases for applications at this time.

evidence.claim: No per-app install cap, user cap, or dev-mode restriction for unreviewed or unlisted Manage apps was found in the Manage docs, rate-limit page, or API changelog.

Probing app.clio.com/oauth/authorize with a deliberately invalid client_id did not return an OAuth error; it redirected through a session flow to a Clio login page, so the endpoint is live but the probe does not show how unknown client IDs are rejected.
evidence.quote: Sign in to Clio Manage Email Next: Password

evidence.claim: The Manage API changelog's entries from 2025 to 2026 (including the 2026-04-08 Multi-Tax release and the 4.0.13 contact-association limit) concern data and API behavior, with no app distribution, install-limit or app-policy change.
evidence.quote: As of version 4.0.13, a Contact can only store 20 email addresses, 20 phone numbers, and 20 physical addresses.

evidence.claim: Clio treats Manage and Platform as separate developer experiences: a Manage integration uses a Manage client application, and a multi-product integration needs both a Manage and a Platform app registration.
evidence.quote: if you want to build a Manage integration, use a Clio Manage client application.

evidence.claim: A free 7-day Clio Manage trial account serves as the test environment; Clio has no separate sandbox.
evidence.quote: Clio does not have a separate sandbox environment. Instead, the 7-day free trial account (Clio Manage)

evidence.claim: A third-party write-up says the Manage API caps requests at 50 per minute per access token during peak hours, which matches Clio's official rate-limit page.
evidence.quote: Clio Manage caps you at 50 requests a minute during peak hours

evidence.claim: Requested permissions are fixed once a user authorizes the app; changing an app's permissions requires prompting users to reauthorize to receive tokens covering the new scopes.
evidence.quote: once a user has authorized your application, their permissions are fixed, even if their token is refreshed.

evidence.claim: Calling an endpoint without the needed permission returns a 403 Forbidden with an error object of type ForbiddenError.
evidence.quote: If you try to access an endpoint without the necessary permissions, The API will return a `403 Forbidden` response.

evidence.claim: Clio's permissions page does not publish a complete list of user capabilities yet and labels it as coming soon; no list of sensitive, restricted or extra-review scopes was found in Clio's Manage docs.
evidence.quote: A complete list of user capabilities is not yet available

evidence.claim: Some Manage endpoints require several permissions together: Personal Injury endpoints need the Personal Injury permission plus Matters, Documents and Contacts, and Clio Payments endpoints need Clio Payments plus Accounting.
evidence.quote: The endpoints require access permissions to "Clio Payments" and "Accounting" to be able to fully utilize the new endpoints.

evidence.claim: Clio's developer guidance asks integrators to request and store only the data their application needs.
evidence.quote: Only request and store information that you require for the purposes of your application.

evidence.claim: Clio's security guidance says developers must track where user data is processed and stored and meet data residency requirements of each region where the app operates.
evidence.quote: Ensure the application meets the data residency requirements of any region where your application operates.

evidence.claim: After the trial, a developer applies for a free developer account; Clio's team reviews the application and converts the trial account if the applicant is eligible.
evidence.quote: Our team will review the application and, if eligible, your trial account will be converted to a developer account.

evidence.claim: Clio Manage private apps are not reviewed by Clio and cannot be published in the App Directory; creating them requires access to a paid Clio account for the app key and secret.
evidence.quote: Private apps for Clio Manage are not reviewed by Clio and cannot be published in Clio's App Directory.

evidence.claim: Apps and integrations, including private apps, are not available on Clio's EasyStart pricing tier.
evidence.quote: Apps and integrations – including private apps – are not available on the EasyStart pricing tier.

evidence.claim: Creating a Manage developer application requires a name, website URL, one or more redirect URIs, acceptance of Developer Terms of Service, and selected app permissions; description, icons, support URL and deauthorization callback are optional.
evidence.quote: Developer Terms of Service | true | You must accept the Developer Terms of Service to build an integration with Clio.

evidence.claim: The app-creation page is developers.clio.com/apps/new, and the App ID shown in the app list is distinct from the App Key (client ID).
evidence.quote: This is not the same value as your App Key mentioned above.

open_questions: Install caps, user limits and dev-mode restrictions for unreviewed or private Manage apps: not found in Clio's docs. Confirm with Clio before relying on a private app for more than your own account.

Whether a free 7-day trial account can create app keys and secrets, or whether a paid account is required (sources say both a trial account is the test environment and that a paid account is needed for keys).
Complete list of Manage access permission names and which are sensitive or restricted: not published; a 'coming soon' note says a full list is not yet available.
Default scopes Composio would request for Clio: unknown because no Composio toolkit was found.
Composio's exact field labels and callback URL location for a custom Clio Manage auth config were not confirmed.
PKCE support for Manage apps: documented for Platform, not confirmed for Manage.
Refresh-token rotation policy: no rule found beyond 'refresh tokens do not expire'.
Redirect URI exact-match rule for Manage is stated only in the Platform docs; treat as exact.
Public listing review timeline: the 2-business-day target comes from a support article of unknown currency.
Developer account approval criteria beyond 'our team will review the application' were not documented.
Regional token and authorize endpoints for EU, CA and AU were seen only in third-party snippets; confirm in Clio's regional docs.
